goals.text: Collect S-K-A-T-E; Collect 5 Pilot Wings; Barrel Hunt; Get 3 Hangtime Gaps; Nosegrind Over the Pipe; Get the Secret Tape (plus stat points, Vicarious Visions logo, alien plushie)

spawn.facing: north, down a dark corridor ramp into the halfpipe room
spawn.notes: LP2 7:24–7:27: the run opens inside a dark corridor; the lit hangar appears beyond it, then the halfpipe's near side ramp fills the view with the S floating above the pipe and the graffiti-covered back wall behind. The arched rail sits dead ahead (PS12). Nothing about either secret area is visible: the helipad is behind a closed west door in the other room, the tunnel behind the east wall. The drop invites one obvious move, a straight air over the halfpipe; LP2 takes the S 5 s after spawn and lands in a manual into barrel B4.

guidance: The roll-in frames the halfpipe, the S and the arched rail in one view: the first goal is shown before the player can steer (LP2 7:24–7:27).
The three hangtime targets are the three biggest silhouettes; the goal text names objects the player already sees.
The helicopter is the only large prop with thin, grindable parts at kicker height; a $50 icon beside it sits on the blade line (VG; LP2 8:20–8:31).
The E hangs over the door that opens. After the trigger, chasing the E puts the open doorway, showing night sky, in front of the player (LP2 8:34–8:36).
The tape is hidden on purpose until the player is outside: it is the only glowing object on a dark pad, ≈ 20 m ahead, above the only ramp (LP2 8:41).
The wind tunnel is advertised by the propeller on the halfpipe's end wall; once open, its cold blue-white light contrasts with the brown hangar (LP2 8:59; LP12 0:40:18 blue).
Barrels sit at ground level beside every landmark (door, glass, start, halfpipe floor and pit) and act as a novice tour; pilot wings sit one step up, on wallride spots, lights and transfers.
designLogic: Spawn-to-letter in 5 seconds: the first letter floats over the centrepiece on the exact line spawn points at, so the first input teaches that the roll-in is a launch (LP2 7:24–7:28).

Each letter sits on a named gap of a different landmark: S on Halfpipe Hangtime, K on Raildrop, A on Wingtip Hangtime, T on Chopper Hop, E on Air Over The Door. Collecting letters teaches the level's gap vocabulary one obstacle at a time.
The tape is a knowledge test, not an execution test: one grind on the helicopter and one easy air. The original's goal list gives no hint that the helicopter is interactive (difficulty 2 once known).
Goals converge on the trigger: 'Hit 3 Hangtime Gaps' sends the player to the helicopter's kickers, the same ramps that reach the blades, and the helicopter's $50 lies on the blade line.
The E is a breadcrumb: it marks the door before it opens and pays the player for looking at it after it opens.
Two secret areas with two jobs: the helipad holds the tape and nothing else, while the wind tunnel holds $250 of the ≈ $450–500 cash plus four gaps. 100% therefore requires discovering both.
Both secrets are opened by an aircraft part (rotor, propeller) on an aircraft-themed prop, so the unlock grammar is learnable inside the level's own fiction.

The secrets extend the long axis at both ends (helipad west, tunnel east), adding ≈ 50% footprint without new routes inside the box. The tunnel continues the halfpipe's channel, so entering it costs no momentum.

Height layering stays close to the floor: kickers, plane wing and blades ≈ 1–2.5 m, vert ≈ 3.5–4 m, raised rails and hanging lights above (estimates). Letters sit at the top of vert airs (S, A, T, E) or on the high rail (K); the lights carry only cash and connections.
Failure is cheap everywhere: every miss lands on open floor or back on the ramp in the same room, and the tape quarter pipe stands on a flat, hazard-free pad.
Density supports single-run completion: LP2 clears all ten goals, the tape and all cash in one 2:00 run (7:23–9:28), with pickups usually less than 10 s apart.

As career level 1 the Hangar introduces the THPS2 secret-area idea (an object trigger opening a hidden room) with the gentlest possible execution; in this study, School II then gates its tape by speed and Venice leaves its tape in plain sight (inference across the three files).
Nosegrind Over The Pipe gates a named trick on the first rail the player sees, teaching that goals can ask for a specific trick, not only a location.
remakeChanges: Score goals: Pro 25,000 → 50,000, Sick 75,000 → 100,000; a High Combo goal (7,500) is added (LP2 checklist vs PS12).
S: the original LP2 run takes it with a halfpipe hangtime; PS12 (1+2) says to grind the arched rail to get it. Probably the same position with a different suggested line (inference).

T: original = a quarter-pipe transfer over the glass divider (Chopper Hop, LP2 8:17); 1+2 = use the quarter pipe to smash through the glass (PS12), and LP12 0:40:30 shows glass shards around Chopper Hop. Breakable glass turns a transfer into a smash-through line.

E: original = over the west door between quarter pipes (VG; the shrine calls it the quarter pipe facing the helicopter); 1+2 = on the giant NEVERSOFT sign over the door, reached by grinding the sign (PS12; LP12 0:40:45). The letter moves onto a grindable sign, making the breadcrumb a rail.

Tape: same trigger and place in both. Grind a blade and the helicopter flies (1+2: crashes out through the wall per Thumbsticks), the door under the sign opens, and the tape is at the top of the snowy quarter pipe. LP12 0:40:48–0:40:51: out the door onto a painted H pad with an orange ring, tape about 2 s later.
Wind tunnel: same propeller trigger (PS12); the remake lights it blue (LP12 0:40:18).

1+2 loads extra collectibles into both secrets: stat points inside the wind tunnel and above the helicopter, the alien plushie in the helipad's left corner, the Vicarious Visions logo above the suspended lights. The secrets' reward value rises without changing their triggers.
Gap names: VG 'Instrument Landing' is 'Instrumental Landing' in PS12; PS12 adds 'Wing To Rail' (500), which has no VG label.
transfer: Rotor-grind gate: make a large landmark machine (crane jib, ceiling fan, rotor) a travelling rail or trick rail reachable from two kickers beside it; grinding it opens a trick gate to an annex. Put the crystal there ≈ 1.5–2.5 m above a small quarter pipe's coping, inside this game's vert-air range.
Breadcrumb over the gate: hang a visible pickup row or crate line directly over the gate that will open, so the player looks at the doorway before and after the unlock.
Goal convergence: if the level has named-air challenges, put one of them on the kickers that reach the trigger so ordinary play parks the player beside the secret.
Opening-line pickup: put a non-crystal collectible over the first halfpipe straight out of spawn, taken with one vert air or spine transfer within 5 s, to teach that the spawn slope is a launch.

Second machine, second annex: a breakable wall at the end of the main halfpipe's axis, opened by grinding a propeller-like trick rail, leading to a lip-trick channel (quarter pipes both ends) as a reward room. Keep it continuous with the halfpipe so momentum carries in.
Keep crystal execution easy and failure cheap when the difficulty is discovery: flat apron, single quarter pipe, no hazards; a miss returns the player to the ramp within 2–3 s.
openQuestions: Original point values of the gaps: only the 1+2 values (PS12) were verified; GameRevolution's original gap list sits behind a bot check and was not used.
When exactly the LP2 player broke the propeller wall: not isolated in 1-s samples (the wall is already open at 8:56).
Whether the helipad door and the wind-tunnel wall stay open across runs in the original (1+2 guides say the School II gym stays open; no statement found for the Hangar).
Is there a $50 icon by the west door that VG does not mark? Evidence for: the LP2 '50 bucks' message at 8:36 and the shrine's $500 cash total against VG's $450. Not seen directly.
All heights are estimates from VG proportions and LP2 frames; no measured values exist.
Which VG pilot-wing icon each LP2 pickup (7:52, 8:08, 8:14, 8:28) corresponds to is only partly established.
